newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sungwon Group plans to sell Midopa shrs.
newsitem.headline: Sungwon Group plans to sell Midopa shrs.

text.p: South Korea's Sungwon Group planned to sell its holding of Midopa Department Store Co Ltd shares, a group official said on Friday.

Sungwon's three affiliates -- Sungwon Corp, Sungwon Finance Co and Daehan Investment Banking Corp -- hold a combined 12.63 percent stake in Midopa, target of a hostile takeover bid by Shindongbang Corp.
"We plan to sell Midopa shares soon. If we miss the right time to liquidate the shares, we will be in a difficult situation," said the official who asked not to be identified.
But he declined to give further details including whether the sales would be made on the open market.

Local newspapers said Sungwon was a majority shareholder friendly to Shindongbang, which told the Korea Stock Exchange last week that it was considering taking over the retailer through public tender.
But the Federation of Korean Industries, representing the interest of large business conglomerates, said it might intervene in the Midopa issue.

The takeover talk sent Midopa shares to a 1997 high of 47,500 won. But as investors began to believe the takeover was impossible, the shares have fallen to their lower limit for five consecutive days.
In Friday morning trading the stock fell 2,200 won to 25,400.
